# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 🫷 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🫷 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 👍]

I can see the full bomb configuration: the display reads 0, the light is yellow, the button is large and says “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and the wires are red, blue, green in positions 1, 2, and 3. I am sending these facts plainly so Blind can use them with the manual; Mute can also hear and confirm them. Mute’s gesture sequence does not provide a sufficiently clear code to decode safely.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb facts: display is 0. Light is yellow. Button is large and marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires by position: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb facts: display is 0. Light is yellow. Button is large and marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires by position: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please relay the manual instruction to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 👍 🫷 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 👍 🫷 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👉 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb remains unchanged. I cannot safely interpret Mute’s gesture sequence because no code was established, and a guessed instruction could detonate the bomb. I am asking Mute to use speech for the exact manual rule so Blind can receive it through the proper channel.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction to Blind, including which action to take and any condition. Gestures are not safely decodable without an agreed code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Do not act until Mute states the exact manual rule in speech.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✌]

I still have no agreed gesture code, so I cannot safely infer the meaning of Mute’s two gestures. The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Blind should wait for Mute’s spoken manual instruction rather than act on an interpretation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Mute just gestured two symbols, down hand then victory hand, but no gesture code has been established. Do not act until you receive the exact manual instruction in speech.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual rule and required action to Blind. Gesture code is not established, so gestures cannot safely convey the instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✌]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute’s repeated gestures may be conveying an instruction, but no code was established, so I must not guess whether they mean a wire or a button action. I am now establishing a simple gesture code with Mute: wire plus position, and explicit button actions. Mute can then resend the manual instruction using that code, and I will speak it to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Establishing code now: 👇 means wire; ☝ means position 1; ✌ means position 2; 🤟 means position 3; 👌 means press button; ✊ means hold button; 🫳 means release button; 👍 means yes; 👎 means no. Please resend the exact manual instruction using this code. Your previous 👇 ✌ is not assumed to mean wire 2 until you resend it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👇", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👌", "✊", "🫳", "👍", "👎"])
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. I am establishing a gesture code with Mute and will relay the exact manual instruction once Mute resends it. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✌]

Mute’s repeated signal now matches the code I established: `👇 ✌` means wire 2. Since wire 2 is blue, I am relaying that the manual’s required wire is the blue wire. Blind should use the manual’s specified wire action on wire 2, without pressing the button unless the manual explicitly requires it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has resent 👇 ✌ under the agreed code: wire 2. Wire 2 is blue. The manual instruction identifies the blue wire, so follow the manual's specified action on wire 2; do not press the button unless the manual explicitly says to.")
wait()
```
